title: Machine-learning-guided lysine dioxygenase variant improves turnover
summary: A structure-based machine-learning mutation-ranking method, combined with molecular dynamics and human rational design, guided variant selection for a lysine dioxygenase. The authors report a five-substitution variant with total turnover number 218 ± 3, compared with 160 ± 2 for wild type in the reported assay. The improvement is specific to this enzyme and assay, not a claim of industrial or therapeutic performance. The source uses conflicting variant abbreviations: its abstract says LPNYI and its Results say LPYNI.
organization: University of Minnesota Twin Cities; University of Texas at Austin

evidence.tested: Primary abstract reports the designed pentamutant’s TTN and wild-type comparator.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and broader application are not established by this bounded review. The source uses conflicting abbreviations for the five-substitution variant.
evidence.ai_role: Structure-based ML prioritized amino-acid substitutions; MD and rational selection also contributed to the final combined variant.

source_review.scope: Primary preprint version and journal methods/results; the variant abbreviation differs between abstract and Results.
